diagnostic_evidence.quote:
for the choice $\theta = \frac12 - \varepsilon$, where $\varepsilon > 0$ can be taken 
        arbitrarily small, there holds $X = H^2_0(\Om) \cap H^{\frac{5}{2} + \varepsilon}(\Om)$.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\theta=\tfrac12-\varepsilon$ one has $H^{-1-\theta}=H^{-3/2+\varepsilon}$ and, by the shift theorem invoked in the paper, $X=\mathcal A^{-1}(H^{-3/2+\varepsilon})=H^2_0\cap H^{5/2+\varepsilon}$, as correctly stated in Remark \ref{remark: assumptions}. Section 4.2.2 instead asserts $X=H^2_0\cap H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ and that the Ritz projection (hence $a_h(\psi,\cdot)$, which involves edge traces of second normal derivatives) is well defined for all $\psi\in H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$; for such $\psi$ the interior penalty form is not well defined, so the claim is false and contradicts the paper's own definition of $X$.

failure_location.quote:
The space $X$ in this case is given by $H^2_0(\Om)\cap H^{\frac52-\varepsilon}(\Om)$.
Hence, the Ritz projection $R_h$ introduced in \eqref{eq:def_ritz_projection} is well defined for any 
$\psi \in H^2_0(\Om)\cap H^{\frac52-\varepsilon}(\Om)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $H^{5/2-\varepsilon}$ by $H^{5/2+\varepsilon}$ in Section 4.2.2, consistent with Remark \ref{remark: assumptions} and Assumption \ref{ass:discrete_bilin_form}.
issues.overall_effect: Only the descriptive claim about the domain of $R_h$ for the $C^0$-IP method is wrong; Theorem \ref{thm:convergence_orders_Czero} uses $\psi\in L^2(I;H^3)$ and is unaffected.
issues.title: Regularity class of X for the C^0 interior penalty method stated with wrong sign of epsilon
issues.why_classification: Local correction of a scope statement; no result or rate depends on the incorrect version.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\tilde \ff$ and $\ff$ only differ by a gradient field, they yield the same velocity solution $\uu$

issues.failure_explanation: The added forcing $10^5(x_1^{-0.49},0)^T$ equals $\nabla q$ with $q=10^5\,x_1^{0.51}/0.51$. The stated pressure $10^5(1.49\,x_1^{1.49})^{-1}$ has gradient $(-10^5 x_1^{-2.49},0)^T$, which is not the perturbation added (and is not even in $L^2$ near $x_1=0$). The claim about the new pressure is therefore false; the correct modified pressure is $\tilde p = p + 10^5 x_1^{0.51}/0.51$.

failure_location.quote: only the pressure changes to $\tilde p = p + 10^5 (1.49 \cdot x_1^{1.49})^{-1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pressure formula by $\tilde p = p + 10^5 x_1^{0.51}/0.51$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the description of the exact pressure in the numerical example is wrong; the velocity solution is indeed unchanged since the perturbation is a gradient, so the experiment and its conclusions are unaffected.
issues.title: Incorrect modified pressure for the gradient-field perturbation in the numerical experiment
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of an ancillary computation with no impact on any theorem, rate, or the numerical results.
